ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: The southern bough is the records’ shortened name for the Southern Bough dream and its vanished dream-world.
EvidenceBody: The ant-kingdom element is stated inside the corpus: Zhean Jingfan's verse says “the Southern Bough ant-hole—enter the dream and travel” (南柯蟻穴，入夢來遊). Baichi Yuan calls his hall activity “all one Southern Bough dream,” while Huqiu Shaolong speaks of getting free of it and seeing human affairs as empty. The name also enters encounter grammar without a story retelling. In Yunmen Wenyan's probing section, after calling an answer a dream, the record supplies several substitute responses, including the bare word “Southern Bough.” Dayu Shouzhi asks what his own dream-talk dreamed and follows with “Southern Bough, ten watches.” The Zen deviation is this compression and redeployment: a literary dream-name becomes a one-word substitute response, the named content of Dayu Shouzhi's dream-talk, and a repeated line in hall addresses and case verses.
